question: The triple point of a phase diagram of a component:

options.opa: Presents 3 degrees of freedom, according to the rule of the phases.
options.opb: Presents 1 degree of freedom, according to the rule of the phases.
options.opc: It is characterized because the liquid and gas phases are indistinguishable.
options.opd: It is characterized because there are three phases in equilibrium.
options.ope: It is characterized because there are four phases in equilibrium.

analysis: The triple point of a phase diagram represents a unique set of conditions where all three phases of a substance (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in equilibrium. At this point, the substance can exist in all three phases simultaneously. This point is characterized by having zero degrees of freedom, as the temperature and pressure are fixed at the triple point conditions.
